purpose: Generated candidates for the Library's Cabinet screen (the whole collection as a grid of boxes, one per species, grouped by clan with spine colours: found bright with portrait and name, met as slate silhouettes, unmet as faint shapes in the mist; a synopsis strip) in art/concept-station/library-cabinet/brief-cabinet.md, with the accepted Pip asset and the species names placed after generation; concept art awaiting the owner's choice.

tool.auth: API key from the environment; not recorded

models.gemini-3-pro-image: Gemini 3 Pro Image: final candidates and refinements

tool.modelChoice: Pro throughout: an exact eight-by-four grid, sixteen distinct silhouettes, empty labels and an exact synopsis strip need it. Round 1: two directions, two fresh each. Round 2: one one-change edit per direction, described in words with no extra reference image.
tool.output: image/jpeg 2752x1536 (16:9 at 2K), kept byte-exact in raw/ for kept candidates; LANCZOS to 1536x864 as the canvas PNG; the screen PNG is the centred 1024:600 band resampled to 1024x600. The Pip asset and then the name layer are placed afterwards (placed/).
tool.imageInputs: Sent as inline image parts, each preceded by a short text part stating its role; the preamble, then the prompt verbatim as the last text part.
tool.budget: At most 20 generations for this screen; 6 used (round 1: 4 fresh, round 2: 2 edits), all on gemini-3-pro-image. No call failed; none was retried.

calls.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Miniature Beasts Station screen concept, the LIBRARY's CABINET screen (the whole collection of species seen at a glance as a cabinet of boxes), a flat screen design that fills the whole 16:9 canvas edge to edge; keep every piece of text at least 60 px inside the left and right edges (the outer 2 percent is bleed, trimmed later to 1024x600). Not a device photograph: no bezel, no buttons, no hands. Design at 1024x600 first: large shapes, few words.
VIBE: the Library of a research instrument, a naturalist's record: quiet, orderly, cool and even light from the upper left, no warm light anywhere (nothing is alive on this screen), crisp edges, clean painted light, soft shadows, no noise or dither. The top bar and bottom line are the instrument's own graphite strips, exactly as on the supplied Home screen: the same smooth sans-serif type (like Inter), the same bolt, diamond and drop counters, the same bottom-line grammar. Pictures lead; the only words are the few listed, each written once.
LAYOUT, as the template. THE CABINET fills the stage: a wall of small specimen drawers in pale, fine-grained wood, the naturalist's own cabinet, eight drawers across and four down in an even grid with thin wooden rails between them, each drawer front a flat box of the same size with a small brass pull and a brass label frame at its foot, and a thin painted spine strip along its left edge in that drawer's own colour exactly as in the template (each of the sixteen a different colour; the lower two rows have no spine strip). The TOP TWO ROWS are the sixteen species, left to right: the first three drawers stand a little open and are FOUND: their label frame holds an empty cream card (nothing written) and their front carries a small painted portrait on cream: the first drawer's portrait area is left EMPTY cream (the creature is placed later); the second shows a round coral fluff under a cap of three flaps; the third a low lagoon-blue lizard with a crest and a tail ending in a glowing bulb, and this third drawer is lifted inside a warm cream focus ring. The fourth drawer is MET: a slate-grey card with the solid slate silhouette of a cat and an empty label frame. The remaining twelve drawers of the top two rows are UNMET: closed, their cards misty slate with a faint silhouette barely darker than the mist, each a different kind seen only as a shape (a fox, a raccoon, a badger, a goat, a big bird, an otter, a turtle, a moth, a beetle, a slug, a standing bulb on root legs, a vertical bolt of lightning), no label frame. The LOWER TWO ROWS are closed blank drawers, plain wood with pulls and no cards or spines, the cabinet's room to grow. Under the drawers a thin slate tray, the SYNOPSIS STRIP: at its left one small engraved word; then a row of sixteen tiny square boxes in a line, the first three filled cream, the fourth filled slate, the other twelve empty hairline squares; then a short thin bar, filled cream for about a fifth of its length; then a row of sixteen tiny upright ticks in the sixteen spine colours, the first four solid and the other twelve thin. Cool, even light from the upper left over the whole cabinet; no lamp, no glow.
TEXT, exactly these and nothing else: top bar left "Library  T5"; top bar centre a yellow lightning bolt "7", a blue diamond "3", a green drop "2"; top bar right "Companion away · with Dot". At the left of the thin strip near the bottom, one small engraved word: "record". Bottom line: orange "✓ Open · ← Home" at left, the middle left EMPTY, grey "a pod waits in the tray" at right. No species names anywhere: every name plate on the boxes is an EMPTY label (names are placed later); no numbers on or near the boxes or the strip; no other words.
Constraints: no digits except the three counters; no letters, numbers, tallies or percentages in the synopsis strip (it is tiny boxes, a bar and ticks only); no species names, the name plates stay empty; the first found box's portrait area is left as a plain, flat, EMPTY cream card (the creature is placed there later); hidden shapes are silhouettes only, no faces, no colours, no detail; no paragraphs, no handwriting, no fake Latin; no people; no living window, no plants, no glow.
calls.preamble: Reference images follow; their roles are stated. Image 1 is the approved Home screen: same device; take its top bar, bottom line, type and counters only. Image 2 is the Library's book, the screen this cabinet opens into: take its paper, ink and the small creature cards' style for the found boxes; its shelf is rejected and nothing of its layout is on this screen. Image 3 is layout truth only: the boxes and labels show where each element sits at 1024x600; it is not a style reference.

the Library's book, the next screen: take its cream paper, ink and the two small species cards' drawing style (the coral fluff under a cap, the lagoon lizard with the glowing tail) for the found boxes; its shelf is rejected and is NOT to be copied, and nothing of its page layout is on this screen

layout truth only: flat boxes at 1024x600 showing the grid of eight columns by four rows (today's sixteen boxes in the top two rows in clan order: three found with empty name plates, one slate met, twelve misty unmet; the lower two rows the empty carcass), the focus ring on the third box, the synopsis strip, and the bottom line; the spine colours are the clans' and are to be kept; not style
